title: Anomaly Detection
tagline: Find the rare and the unusual: statistical outliers, distance and density methods, isolation forests, one-class SVMs, autoencoders, fraud with imbalanced data, and explaining why a point was flagged.
prereqs: Machine Learning. Deep Learning for the autoencoder step; Time Series & Forecasting helps there too.

steps.title: What anomaly detection is
steps.why: Kinds of anomalies, and why you usually train on mostly normal data.

steps.title: Outliers by z-score
steps.why: Flag points far from the mean, which works best on roughly normal data.

steps.title: Multivariate outliers with Mahalanobis distance
steps.why: Distance that accounts for correlation; assumes a roughly elliptical data cloud.

steps.title: Outliers as DBSCAN noise points
steps.why: Points in no dense cluster become noise, a simple outlier signal.

steps.title: Local outlier factor
steps.why: Compare a point's density to its neighbors' to find local outliers.

steps.title: Isolation forest
steps.why: Anomalies tend to need fewer random splits to isolate, coded in Python.

steps.title: One-class SVM
steps.why: Learn a boundary around normal-only data and flag what falls outside it.

steps.title: LSTM autoencoder for time-series anomalies
steps.why: Train on normal sequences, then flag windows with high reconstruction error.

steps.title: Fraud detection with imbalanced data
steps.why: Credit card fraud with under 1% positives: resampling and the right metrics.

steps.title: Explain anomalies with SHAP
steps.why: See which features pushed an isolation forest to flag a point.

steps.title: Where the field stands
steps.why: A Microsoft Research talk on algorithms, benchmarks, and explaining anomalies.

projects: Compare z-score, LOF, and isolation forest on a public credit card fraud dataset using PR-AUC.
Build an LSTM autoencoder that flags unusual windows in server CPU or sensor data, and plot the alerts.
For the top 20 flagged points of any detector, show a SHAP explanation of why each was flagged.
